blocks.content: Spotting exam traps requires reading the question stem twice and actively searching for qualifier words before selecting an answer.

rows: Treat absolute assertions with high skepticism
Circle or underline negative words in the stem immediately
Option resembles the correct answer but contains a minor flaw
Read all four options completely before making a choice

items: Questions asking for 'NOT CORRECT' options remain the single highest source of avoidable negative marks.
In factual statements, closely inspect numbers, dates, and ministry names as examiner traps frequently interchange them.
Never mark the first plausible option immediately; always evaluate all four choices to rule out look-alike traps.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Extreme modifiers such as 'always', 'never', and 'only' usually render a statement false in competitive examinations.
Always highlight keywords like 'NOT CORRECT', 'INCORRECT', or 'EXCEPT' in the question stem before looking at options.
Partial-truth traps combine a correct fact with an incorrect detail to mislead superficial readers.
Time-sink questions are intentionally placed to break your pacing; skip and revisit them during your second pass.
